source.title: Some problems concerning the structure of random walk paths

accepted.question_text: For a simple symmetric random walk on the two-dimensional integer lattice, starting at the origin and moving at each step with equal probability to one of the four neighboring lattice points, characterize the growth rates of functions f(n) for which the following event occurs almost surely: for all sufficiently large n, by time f(n) the random walk has visited every lattice point whose Euclidean distance from the origin is less than n. What necessary and sufficient conditions on f(n) determine whether this eventual covering of each disk of radius n happens?

evidence.quote: Consider an infinite random walk in d-dimensional space. The paths may be represented as sequences of lattice points in the d-dimensional square lattice...

There is a related problem which we have not been able to solve. What can be said about functions f(n) such that every lattice point within a distance n of the origin has been visited before the f(n)th step for all n>n0.

accepted.question_text: For a simple symmetric random walk in d-dimensional integer lattice space with d >= 3, let the distance process record how far the walker is from the origin, and let the eventual escape radius from time n onward be the smallest distance from the origin attained at any time after n. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on comparison functions that give valid eventual upper bounds for this escape-radius function, analogous in strength to known necessary and sufficient upper-bound results for laws of the iterated logarithm.
accepted.context_brief: Escape-rate upper bounds in transient random walks

evidence.quote: We ask: How large a sphere with centre the origin can we be certain that Sd(n) remains outside it for n >= n0?

We are unable to obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for upper bounds to the function c,,(n) which would correspond to the known results obtained by the first author [4] or Feller [6] for the law of the iterated logarithm.

accepted.question_text: For a simple symmetric random walk on the two-dimensional integer lattice, let T_2(n) be the maximum number of times that any single lattice point is visited during the first n steps. Determine the exact almost-sure asymptotic behavior of T_2(n) when it is normalized by (log n)^2; in particular, decide whether the normalized maximum multiplicity has the almost-sure limit suggested by the source after its proved lower and upper bounds.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum local time in planar random walk

trace.notes: Input normalized as a zbMATH resolver URL with document id 3148784.

The zbMATH web page returned a Cloudflare challenge, so the zbMATH API was used only as resolver metadata. The API identified DOI 10.1007/BF02020631, title, authors, journal, and year. A readable exact-title PDF was downloaded from an Erdos archive URL after a local SSL validation failure required a certificate-validation-disabled retry.

Mapped the PDF as a 26-page article. Main structure: introductory random-walk setup; Sections 1-3 on returns to the origin and planar recurrence estimates; Section 4 on distance from the origin and escape rates; Section 5 on multiplicities of visited points; final remarks around unresolved covering, escape-bound, multiplicity-distribution, and maximum-multiplicity questions.
